sources.entry: IHateMoney - Manage your shared expenses, easily. (Demo, Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Docker/Python
I Hate Money | Simple shared-budget manager to split expenses with friends

summary.one_liner: I Hate Money (ihatemoney) is a web application for tracking shared expenses among a group, recording who paid for what and for whom, and helping settle the bills.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web app for managing shared budgets: it keeps track of who bought what, when, and for whom, and helps settle the bills. It supports SQLite, PostgreSQL, MariaDB (10.3.2 or above), and an in-memory backend. It runs on Python 3.11 to 3.13, and a Docker installation is offered. The README says the project aims for simplicity, with minimal JavaScript, few dependencies, and no need for invited people to create accounts. The maintainers state the project is moving into a "maintenance mode," prioritizing stability over major new features. A hosted version and cloud provider options are linked, along with online documentation and a mailing list.
how_to_run: Docker installation is offered (see the online documentation for details)
notable: No account needed for people you invite; same web interface on mobile
Deliberately minimal JavaScript and small codebase
Hosted version available, with donations used to maintain it
Started in 2011; now in a maintenance-focused phase
caveats: Project is moving toward maintenance mode; new features must fit simplicity goals
Contributor energy is lower than in the past, per the README
Officially targets the current Debian stable and the previous release; other environments may be less supported
